approval_field_interpretation.algorithm: Remove parenthesized qualifiers and nonletters from the extracted headword; all-uppercase letters yield approved, other letters yield not-approved, and no letters yield unknown.
approval_field_interpretation.limitation: Retained verbatim as raw mechanical source status only; not an IT disposition, verified typography, or blanket permission for any sense.

sequence.selection: Consecutive source rows 1721 through 1760, without filtering by status, domain, warnings, or disposition.
sequence.order_basis: pdf_page ascending, then numeric row suffix of the stable entry ID; extractor assigns suffixes from positioned row anchors in page order.

interpretation.disposition_scope: Each disposition applies only to the stated sense and scope, and remains a draft editorial proposal. Allowed and restricted do not constitute vocabulary approval.
interpretation.allowed: Proposed for the stated sense, subject to editorial review.
interpretation.restricted: Proposed only for the explicitly stated sense and contextual constraints.
interpretation.prohibited: Proposed exclusion of the stated prose use; choose a contextually correct alternative.
interpretation.not-applicable: No general IT prose sense proposed for the source sense; this does not ban all specialist physical documentation.
interpretation.needs-review: Mechanical ambiguity prevents a settled decision; definitions and examples are provisional editorial proposals.
interpretation.alternatives: Original contextual expressions, not allocated term IDs or an assertion that each expression is globally approved; use only when it preserves the intended meaning.
interpretation.examples: All examples and explanations are original IT-STE editorial content. Positive examples may demonstrate a replacement rather than use a prohibited or inapplicable headword. Positive examples under needs-review are provisional.
interpretation.literal_boundary: No decision authorizes changing literal code, API fields, protocol tokens, UI labels, citations, or proper names. No unknown proper noun is approved by this batch.
interpretation.source_content_limit: Only short headwords, raw status, locators, and extraction warnings are retained from source rows; source definitions, alternatives, and examples are not reproduced.

decisions.it_definition: Handle HTTP requests for files under a configured URL-to-file mapping and send the applicable HTTP response to the requesting client.
decisions.rationale: Authenticated page 374 shows a serves-to-control construction, not an HTTP definition. Restrict this independently supported IT adaptation to HTTP file-request handling under an explicit mapping. Python documents file serving, HEAD, conditional responses and errors; serving does not imply a successful content-body transfer for every request, secure filesystem containment or production suitability. Generic purpose/function wording still needs an accurate verb. See docs/it-ste-research/W1-D-P374.md.
permitted_contextual_alternatives: handle HTTP requests for the mapped files
send the specified file contents, when the response includes that body

positive.text: The HTTP handler serves files using the configured URL-to-file mapping.
positive.explanation: Names the HTTP role and resource mapping, not a guarantee of successful delivery. The actual method and status determine whether file contents are sent; this is not an instruction to deploy Python http.server in production.

problematic.text: Serve the system.
problematic.explanation: Does not identify content, recipient, or function.

mechanical_ambiguities: Source contains an editorial instruction rather than a definition; network-serving scope is not established.

decisions.it_definition: Provisionally, the condition of meeting a hardware component's operating requirements.
decisions.rationale: Authenticated page 374 resolves the overlap: SERVICEABLE belongs to this noun row; Correct or satisfactory belongs to the next adjective row. Lenovo's fan procedure establishes seating and installation constraints, not a complete operating-acceptance criterion. Keep needs-review until a named hardware component's full applicable requirements and the intended noun scope are established; selected checks alone do not prove general fitness or future reliability. See docs/it-ste-research/W1-D-P374.md.

positive.text: Record whether the replacement fan passes its operating checks.
positive.explanation: Records only the named checks' result; the applicable procedure must identify them and their limits. Passing selected checks is not proof of every operating requirement, future reliability or complete serviceability.

problematic.text: Serviceability means there can be no future failure.
problematic.explanation: Current fitness does not guarantee future reliability.

mechanical_ambiguities: Definition includes Correct or satisfactory, apparently overlapping the following adjective row.
